glyph_origin: Early bronze inscriptions: Pictogram (象形) – acorn. Original form of 皂 through an intermediate variant 皁 (once also written as 草). Borrowed phonetically for "morning" sense. Late bronze inscriptions: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 日 (“sun”) + phonetic 棗, with 棗 sometimes simplified as 朿. Small seal script: Ideogrammic compound (會意): 日 (“sun”) + 甲 (“first”) – when the sun first rises. However, Xu Shen's interpretation is not based on oracle bones and bronzes inscriptions. In some ancient texts, 蚤 was often used instead. Unrelated to the ancient version of 是: in this character, it doesn't represent an acorn but a spoon.
senses: [zǎo] long ago; for a long time
